setup.description: Create a feature branch on the DataCopilot repo (213) for eval runs. Pass the branch ID to each eval prompt. The branch's own userConfig singleton is edited in place; teardown discards it with the branch.
setup.command: dxs source branch create --repo 213 --title "user-config-editor-eval-{timestamp}" --description "Temporary branch for user-config-editor skill evals"

evals.name: nested-setting-and-set-with-spread
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: users want the app to remember their default warehouse and default owner. Add a per-user setting for this to the package's user configuration, then write the save-side flow code for a preferences form that stores both values — including what happens when the user clears the owner field and saves.
evals.expected_output: The own userConfig row's settings[] gains one type:object descriptor (e.g. defaults) whose objectTypeDef holds warehouse_id and owner_id number descriptors; validate runs before the write; the consumer code reads defensively and saves with read-then-set() spreading the current object, omitting cleared keys rather than relying on update() with null.
expectations: The own userConfig row is located by applicationId == branch id and isExternal == false (or by a bare 'get userconfig userConfig' whose returned id/applicationId is checked) — no dependency package's row is edited
The edited body keeps referenceName "userConfig", configurationTypeId 37 and title "User configuration" unchanged, and its id is the own row's id (not 0)
settings[] contains a descriptor with type "object" whose objectTypeDef holds warehouse_id and owner_id descriptors with type "number" and isCollection false
All new setting ids are snake_case
The consumer save code calls $userSettings.<Package>.get() and then $userSettings.<Package>.set({ ...current, ... }) — the spread of the current object is present
Clearing the owner is handled by omitting (or deleting) the key before set(), and the response states that update() with a null value would not clear it
The consumer read code uses optional chaining or a null-coalescing default (e.g. settings?.defaults?.warehouse_id ?? null)
The userConfig description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate userconfig' run before 'dxs configuration upsert userconfig' (or before the documented fallback write)

evals.name: refuse-second-userconfig
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: create a new userConfig component called reporting_user_config with a boolean setting compact_mode so each user can toggle a compact report layout.
evals.expected_output: The agent declines to create a second user configuration, explains that every package has exactly one fixed-name userConfig singleton, and instead adds compact_mode as a boolean descriptor to the own row's settings[] after validate.
expectations: No 'dxs configuration create userconfig' command is run, and no body with a referenceName other than "userConfig" is pushed
The response explains that userConfig is a per-package singleton with the fixed referenceName "userConfig" that cannot be created or renamed
The response offers or performs the alternative: adding compact_mode to the existing own row's settings[]
If the edit is performed, the compact_mode descriptor has type "boolean" and isCollection false, and existing settings are preserved
The userConfig description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
If a write is performed, 'dxs configuration validate userconfig' runs before 'dxs configuration upsert userconfig'

evals.name: same-branch-schema-and-consumer
evals.prompt: On connection 9, branch {branch_id}: a teammate will build a form on another branch that reads $userSettings.<Package>.get() and uses settings.last_report_id. Add the last_report_id setting here so they can start. Is there anything they need to know about which branch their form must live on?
evals.expected_output: The agent adds a number descriptor last_report_id to the own userConfig and explains that I<Package>UserSettings is regenerated per branch, so the consumer form must land on the same branch as the schema change (or wait for publish when consuming cross-package), otherwise it fails validate with Property 'last_report_id' does not exist on type 'I<Package>UserSettings'.
expectations: settings[] gains a last_report_id descriptor with type "number"
The response states that the generated interface I<Package>UserSettings is regenerated per branch from the userConfig schema

The response states that the consumer form and the schema change must land on the same branch, and names the failure mode (validate error: Property 'last_report_id' does not exist on type 'I<Package>UserSettings')
The response does not claim the setting becomes visible to other branches as soon as it is written
The userConfig description is non-empty and at most 100 characters
The transcript contains 'dxs configuration validate userconfig' run before 'dxs configuration upsert userconfig' (or before the documented fallback write)
